title: Nuclear Excitation by Inelastic Positron Scattering in Hydrogenlike $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{89+}$ Ions
summary: We develop a relativistic theory of nuclear excitation by inelastic positron scattering (NEIPS) with nuclear hyperfine mixing (NHM) explicitly included and apply it to hydrogenlike $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{89+}$ ions. The target ion is described by dressed hyperfine states, while the incident and outgoing positron continuum states are treated within a relativistic distorted-wave approach. We calculate hyperfine-resolved excitation cross sections for incident positron energies from $10^{2}$ to $10^{5}~\mathrm{eV}$. The cross sections increase strongly with the positron energy, with the $F_g=2\rightarrow F_e=2$ channel exhibiting the largest value. Comparison with NEIPS of the bare $^{229}\mathrm{Th}^{90+}$ nucleus shows that NHM enhances the excitation cross sections by about four orders of magnitude. These results demonstrate that NHM provides an efficient mechanism for enhancing NEIPS and broaden the range of nuclear excitation processes in which NHM plays a significant role.

title: Lightest $Ω$-baryon systems with strangeness $-3$ and $-6$ within the framework of Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations
summary: We investigate the binding energies and spatial properties of few-body $Ω$-baryon systems with strangeness $S=-3$ and $S=-6$ using the configuration-space Faddeev and Faddeev--Yakubovsky equations. For the first time, microscopic Faddeev--Yakubovsky calculations are performed for the four- and five-body $ΩNNN$, $ΩNNNN$, and $ΩΩNN$ systems. We employ HAL QCD and meson-exchange $ΩN$ interactions, together with the HAL QCD $ΩΩ$ potential, and examine the effects of Coulomb interactions and spin--isospin configurations. The calculations predict substantial enhancement of binding with increasing baryon number, with the most strongly bound $ΩNNNN$ configurations reaching approximately $60$~MeV and bound $ΩΩNN$ states in the $S=-6$ sector. The results reveal pronounced spin dependence and compact few-body structures, with the $Ω$ baryon preferentially localized near the center-of-mass. These findings provide new predictions for light multistrange nuclear systems and extend microscopic few-body calculations into the four- and five-body $Ω$-baryon sectors.

title: Total kinetic energy of fission fragments within time-dependent density functional theory: role of particle-number projection and collective deformations
summary: Time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations of fission fragment total kinetic energy (TKE), restricted to axially symmetric trajectories and a single symmetry-violating mean-field state, underestimate TKE by 10-20 MeV away from the most probable mass split. We reexamine this for $^{240}$Pu and $^{252}$Cf within relativistic TDDFT+BCS, combining particle-number projection (PNP) with an extended collective space including hexadecapole and non-axial deformations. Varying the pairing strength leaves the TKE essentially unchanged, but PNP converts each trajectory into a resolved TKE distribution over fragment mass, and the enlarged collective space is needed to reach the correct scission configurations. Together, these reproduce the empirical TKE mass dependence substantially better than standard calculations, indicating the discrepancy reflects missing symmetry restoration and configuration space rather than a deficient energy functional.

title: Neural Network Potential Reconstruction from Phase Shifts in Resonant $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ Scattering
summary: We reconstruct a local, energy-independent effective potential for the narrow $D_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+{}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ from elastic phase shifts, using a Gaussian-enveloped neural parametrization coupled to a differentiable variable-phase calculation and checked by independent radial Schrödinger solvers. For the first resonance (below $2.5$ MeV LAB), the reconstruction gives a $90^\circ$ crossing at $1.001$ MeV LAB and a derivative width of $85$ keV LAB. The published Dubovichenko potential gives similar values with its original kinetic coefficient. Four reconstructions with adjustable range place the crossing within $5$ keV of one another while their central potentials span $47$ MeV. This spread illustrates the radial ambiguity of the inversion for the measured $D_{3/2}$ phases. The broad $P_{3/2}$ resonance of $n+α$ serves as a benchmark for the same method.

title: Background characterization in the PIKACHU Phase 1 search for two-neutrino double-beta decay of $^{160}$Gd
summary:
We report a background characterization for the search for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u2β$) decay of $^{160}$Gd using Ce:Gd$_3$Al$_2$Ga$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillators in the PIKACHU experiment Phase 1 at the Kamioka underground laboratory. The experimental backgrounds were investigated through delayed-coincidence analysis and spectral fitting based on GEANT4 simulations. In particular, surface contamination of the crystal was identified through the characteristic distortion of the $^{214}$Po $α$-ray spectrum, leading to an improved background model that reproduces the observed energy spectra. No significant excess attributable to $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay was observed, yielding a lower limit of $T^{2ν}_{1/2} \geq 2.32 	imes 10^{19}$ yr at 90\% C.L. The established background model and analysis framework provide a foundation for future PIKACHU phases aiming to discover $^{160}$Gd $2
u2β$ decay.

title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables; submitted to Phys. Rev. C
summary: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $λ_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.
